Overview & Dates

Choose your entry

Start with the route that matches your education and career stage. Always confirm age, medical and stream eligibility in the active notice.

NDA & Naval Academy

The officer-entry route after Class 12. The written exam has Mathematics and the General Ability Test, followed by SSB and medical examination.

  • Written paperMaths 300 + GAT 600
  • Duration2½ hours each
  • Questions120 Maths + 150 GAT
  • InterviewSSB: 900 marks
  • Penalty⅓ of question marks

What to prioritise

Maths: algebra, matrices, trigonometry, coordinate geometry, calculus, vectors, statistics and probability.

GAT: English (200) plus physics, chemistry, general science, history, geography and current events (400).

Army wing requires Class 12; Navy, Air Force and INAC routes require the science/PCM conditions stated in the notification.

Combined Defence Services

Graduate officer entry for IMA, INA, AFA and OTA. IMA/INA/AFA candidates write English, GK and Elementary Mathematics; OTA candidates write English and GK.

  • IMA / INA / AFA3 × 100 marks
  • OTA2 × 100 marks
  • Duration2 hours per paper
  • After writtenSSB + medical

Best use of time

Build accuracy in English and arithmetic first: these improve through daily drills. Keep GK revision short but frequent. For OTA, use the saved mathematics block for extra English and current-affairs practice.

Degree and subject requirements differ by academy. AFA and INA have specific degree/10+2 conditions; check the active UPSC notice.

Air Force Common Admission Test

  • Online test100 questions / 300 marks
  • Duration2 hours
  • Scoring+3 correct · −1 wrong
  • SectionsGA, English, Maths, Reasoning
  • Next stageAFSB + medical

Branch lens

Flying: numerical speed, spatial reasoning and a calm AFSB performance matter.

Ground Duty: technical and non-technical branches have different degree criteria.

Technical: verify whether the current notice includes any separate technical testing or branch-specific qualification.

AFCAT rules can change by cycle. Treat the active IAF notification as final.

Army Agniveer

Category-specific online Common Entrance Examination, followed by recruitment rally stages, document checks and medical examination.

  • General Duty50 questions / 100
  • Technical50 questions / 200
  • Clerk / Store Keeper50 questions / 200
  • Core subjectsGK, science, maths, reasoning

Category strategy

GD: broad accuracy across GK, science and maths.

Technical: physics, chemistry and mathematics carry the load.

Clerk/SKT: English is the largest block; computer basics and part-wise qualifying rules matter.

Question mix and qualifying requirements vary by category.

Navy Agniveer SSR / MR

  • SSR100 questions / 60 min
  • SSR subjectsEnglish, science, maths, GA
  • MR50 questions / 30 min
  • MR subjectsScience & maths, GA
  • Penalty0.25 per wrong answer

Sea-service preparation

For SSR, practise one-minute questions: the paper rewards immediate recall and clean calculation. For MR, revise Class 10 science and arithmetic in mixed sets. Both routes require physical and medical qualification.

The 2026 pattern also includes SSR (Medical), with English, science, biology and general awareness.

Air Force Agniveervayu

Phase-I is an objective, bilingual online test (except English). Paper length depends on the chosen subject stream.

  • SciencePhysics, maths, English · 60 min
  • Other than scienceEnglish + RAGA · 45 min
  • Both streamsAll sections · 85 min
  • Penalty0.25 per wrong answer

What follows

Shortlisted candidates move to document verification, physical fitness, adaptability tests and medical examination. Science candidates should work from 10+2 physics and mathematics; non-science candidates should prioritise English, reasoning and general awareness.

Syllabus

Selection map

Different entries vary, but the journey usually follows this sequence.

01Written / online testAccuracy, speed, syllabus coverage and smart question selection.
02ScreeningSSB Stage I or service-specific shortlisting and document verification.
03AssessmentSSB/AFSB tasks, rally fitness or adaptability tests, depending on entry.

Study Material

Core study library

High-yield notes for the overlapping written syllabus. Tap a subject and revise from the page.

Arithmetic essentials

  • Percentage change: new value = old × (1 ± rate/100).
  • Successive changes a%, b%: net = a + b + ab/100 (use signs).
  • Average = total ÷ count. If one value changes by d, average changes by d/n.
  • Profit% and loss% are calculated on cost price, not selling price.
SI = PRT/100 · Amount = P(1 + r/100)^n for annual CI

Time, work & motion

  • If A finishes in x days, one-day work = 1/x.
  • Together: 1/T = 1/x + 1/y.
  • Distance = speed × time; convert km/h to m/s by × 5/18.
  • Relative speed: add in opposite directions; subtract in same direction.
Average speed for equal distances = 2uv/(u+v)

Algebra & trigonometry

  • (a+b)² = a²+2ab+b²; (a−b)² = a²−2ab+b².
  • For ax²+bx+c=0: roots = (−b ± √(b²−4ac))/2a.
  • sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
  • sin(A±B)=sinA cosB ± cosA sinB.
Area of triangle = ½ab sin C · Heron: √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]

Geometry, calculus & probability

  • Circle: circumference 2πr; area πr².
  • Sphere: surface 4πr²; volume 4πr³/3.
  • d(xⁿ)/dx = nxⁿ⁻¹; ∫xⁿdx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)+C.
  • P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B).
Slope m=(y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁) · line: y−y₁=m(x−x₁)

Agreement

  • Each, every, either, neither take a singular verb: “Each cadet is ready.”
  • With either…or / neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
  • “A number of” takes plural; “the number of” takes singular.
  • Collective nouns are singular when the group acts as one unit.

Tense control

  • Use simple past for a finished time: “The unit arrived yesterday.”
  • Use present perfect for an unfinished period or present result.
  • In reported speech, backshift when the reporting verb is past—unless the fact remains universally true.
  • After “did,” use the base verb: “did not go,” never “did not went.”

Vocabulary through structure

RootMeaningExample
benegoodbeneficial

dictspeakverdict
circumaroundcircumnavigate

Comprehension drill

  • Read the question stem before rereading the passage.
  • Separate author’s claim from examples and evidence.
  • Reject options that are true generally but unsupported by the passage.
  • For tone, choose the least exaggerated defensible word.

Mechanics

  • Newton I: inertia; II: F=ma; III: forces occur in equal, opposite pairs on different bodies.
  • Momentum p=mv; impulse equals change in momentum.
  • Work W=Fs cosθ; power P=W/t; kinetic energy = ½mv².
  • At constant acceleration: v=u+at; s=ut+½at²; v²=u²+2as.

Electricity & optics

  • Ohm’s law: V=IR. Series resistances add; parallel reciprocals add.
  • Electrical power P=VI=I²R=V²/R.
  • Mirror/lens relation: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u under the adopted sign convention.
  • Refractive index n=c/v; light bends toward the normal on entering a denser medium.

Chemistry

  • Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons.
  • Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain.
  • pH below 7 acidic, 7 neutral, above 7 basic at room conditions.
  • One mole contains 6.022 × 10²³ entities.

Biology & environment

  • Mitochondria release usable energy; ribosomes build proteins.
  • Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins return it.
  • Vaccination trains adaptive immunity using antigens.
  • Food-chain energy decreases at higher trophic levels; matter cycles, energy flows.

Constitution quick sheet

  • Fundamental Rights: Part III; Directive Principles: Part IV; Fundamental Duties: Part IVA.
  • President is constitutional head; Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.
  • Money Bills originate only in Lok Sabha.
  • Article 32 protects the right to constitutional remedies.

Modern India

  • 1857: widespread uprising; Crown rule followed in 1858.
  • Indian National Congress founded in 1885.
  • Non-Cooperation: 1920; Civil Disobedience: 1930; Quit India: 1942.
  • Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949; in force 26 Jan 1950.

Geography anchors

  • Southwest monsoon has Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches.
  • Himalayan rivers are largely perennial; Peninsular rivers depend more on rainfall.
  • Black soil suits cotton; alluvial soil dominates northern plains.
  • Coriolis effect deflects moving air right in Northern Hemisphere.

Defence literacy

  • Know service commands, ranks, training academies and tri-service organisations.
  • Track major exercises by countries involved and service type—not just names.
  • For current affairs, record event, actors, location, purpose and one strategic implication.
  • Revise official updates monthly; dated current affairs cannot remain “current” forever.

Series & analogy

  • Check first differences, then second differences, ratios and alternating terms.
  • For letters, map A=1…Z=26 and test shifts.
  • In analogies, name the relation before viewing options.
  • For odd-one-out, identify the rule shared by exactly three items.

Coding & directions

  • Test direct shifts, reverse alphabet, pair swaps and word reversal.
  • Draw direction questions on a coordinate cross; never solve mentally.
  • Facing north: right=east, left=west. Rotate the frame after every turn.
  • Net displacement uses Pythagoras only after horizontal and vertical totals.

Syllogism discipline

  • “All A are B” does not mean “all B are A.”
  • “Some” means at least one, not all.
  • Two negative premises produce no valid conclusion.
  • Use simple Venn circles; accept only conclusions forced in every valid diagram.

Spatial reasoning

  • For paper folding, unfold in reverse order and mirror each fold.
  • Opposite faces on a cube never meet along an edge.
  • Count rotations by tracking one fixed reference feature.
  • In embedded figures, ignore orientation and scale unless specified.

Practice

Diagnostic test

15 mixed questions. One point each. No penalty here—use the explanations to find your weakest area.

—/15

Answer every question, then submit. Your result stays only for this visit.

SSB practice room

SSB is not a personality costume. Practise clear observation, usable ideas, teamwork and honest reflection.

PPDT in 4 minutes

Observe for 30 seconds. Note characters, mood and action. Write a realistic story with a clear protagonist, practical plan, teamwork and measurable outcome. Then narrate in under one minute.

TAT story frame

Situation → goal → obstacles → organised action → result. Avoid miracles, melodrama and unsupported heroics. Show initiative without making everyone else passive.

WAT response

Write the first constructive, grammatically complete thought. Do not force moral slogans. “Risk” could become: “Calculated risk follows preparation and backup planning.”

Interview ledger

Prepare truthful examples for responsibility, conflict, failure, improvement, teamwork and decision-making. Know your education, family context, hobbies and reasons for choosing the service.

Group discussion: a useful speaking pattern

Enter with one grounded point, add evidence or an example, connect to another candidate’s useful idea, and invite the group toward a conclusion. Volume is not leadership.

Lecturette: 3-minute structure

Open with a definition and relevance. Use three ordered points, one example, one counterpoint and a brief conclusion. Practise with a timer; do not memorise ornate openings.

What not to manufacture

Do not invent achievements, rehearse a false “ideal officer” persona or hide obvious weaknesses behind clichés. Consistency across psychological tests, interview and group tasks matters.

Study Plan

12-week battle plan

Six study days, one test-and-review day. Repeat weak topics, not familiar ones.

Weeks 1–4

Build the base

  • 90 min core subject
  • 45 min English / reasoning
  • 30 min GK revision
  • 20 min running + mobility
  • One sectional test weekly
Weeks 5–8

Increase pressure

  • Mixed timed sets
  • Error notebook by topic
  • Two full sections weekly
  • One PPDT story + narration
  • Progressive run intervals
Weeks 9–12

Simulate selection

  • Two full mocks weekly
  • OMR / CBT discipline
  • Revise only marked gaps
  • Interview speaking drills
  • Taper before exam day
Rule

Every wrong answer must become one line in an error log: concept missed → why I chose it → rule that fixes it. Reattempt those questions after 48 hours and again after one week.

Physical readiness

Train above the minimum gradually. Official standards differ by entry, category and notification.

Starter week × 4

  1. Mon: easy 20–30 min run + mobility
  2. Tue: push-ups, squats, rows, plank—3 rounds
  3. Wed: 6 × 200 m controlled intervals
  4. Thu: walk, stretch, sleep focus
  5. Fri: tempo run + core
  6. Sat: timed 1.6 km every second week
  7. Sun: full recovery

Progress without injury

Increase weekly running volume by no more than roughly 10% when your body is adapting well. Use shoes that fit, warm up before fast work, and keep at least one recovery day.

Stop and seek qualified medical advice for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, or persistent bone/joint pain. Medical eligibility is decided by the relevant service—not by this guide.
